newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat called to open one to two cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat called to open one to two cents higher.

text.p: CBOT wheat futures were called to open one to two cents per bushel higher on a technical recovery plus a slower-than-usual wheat harvest pace, traders said.
USDA Monday reported the U.S. winter wheat harvest as of Sunday at 24 percent complete, below the 38 percent of a year ago and behind the 35-percent average for that time of year.
There were some reports that showers would slow wheat harvest Tuesday but cash dealers said most of the rain was in eastern Kansas and not in the key wheat growing counties.

Also traders said a slight decline in spring wheat conditions was supportive to the market. USDA Monday said as of Sunday, 50 percent of spring crop was in good to excellent condition, down from 52 percent in that category the previous week.
CBOT's Project A overnight trend for wheat was 3/4 to two cents higher.
